scope: Native make_tuple/2 size validation, empty singleton and repeated-value construction with owned GC/resource boundaries.
adaptations: Require a small count in 0..MAX_ARITYVAL; other counts are badarg. For zero, return an immutable Engine-owned, namespace-free two-word literal empty tuple, including native read-ahead padding. Worlds/processes retain the Engine; no per-call allocation or pinning is needed.

For positive counts, precharge header/fill work, reserve words plus existing primitive heap credit, reload the rooted fill value after collection and publish the completed tuple last. Each slot contains the same term reference, not a deep copy. Quota/work/OOM outcomes remain distinct; the runtime heap bound can refuse a natively valid large count.

Tests exercise actual compiled calls, zero under allocator/quota denial and full heap, heap/refcounted binary aliasing, moving GC, badarg classes, the native maximum-plus-one boundary, resource refusal at the valid maximum, all primitive work/allocation prefixes, source/credit preservation and final balance. A live peer retains the singleton across another World's reclamation and GC. Shared-worker tests cover exact/one-below work, reuse and reclamation. No successful maximum-sized tuple allocation is claimed.
